proposals.current_remark: **The m-regime alone is insufficient.** Take the singleton class $\mathcal P=\{P\}$ with $P=\delta_0$, target $\theta(P)=0$, statistic $T_k(z_1,\ldots,z_k)=1/k$, and normalization $a_k=k$. Let $m_n=\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor$. For all $n\ge4$, $1\le m_n<n$, and $m_n\to\infty$, $m_n/n\to0$, and $a_{m_n}/a_n=m_n/n\to0$. The actual size-$n$ and size-$m_n$ roots are both identically $1$, so their CDFs $J_{n,P}$ and $H_{m_n,P}$ coincide exactly. For either resampling method, every resampled statistic is $1/m_n$, so $\widehat H_{m,n}$ is the point-mass CDF at $1-m_n/n$. With $\alpha_1=\alpha_2=1/4$, both quantiles equal $1-m_n/n$ and $I_n=\{m_n/n^2\}$. Since $m_n/n^2>0$, the coverage of $\theta(P)=0$ is zero for every $n\ge4$. Thus uniform CDF approximation of the actual m-root by the feasible resampling root, and the associated quantile coverage guarantee, do not follow from the m-regime even when the actual n-root and m-root laws coincide.
